description:
Cron HEARTBEAT that (re)starts the singleton importer-poll drainer for the LLM session ledger across ALL registered PULLING sources. Each fire does ZERO importing on the action-queue thread: it submits ONE background poll pass to a single-slot executor (separate from the auto-summarize and event-embedding slots, so the three drains run independently) and returns in milliseconds with `{"poller": "started"}`, or `{"poller": "already_running"}` if a drainer already holds the slot (that fire is a no-op). At most one importer-poll drainer runs at a time PER PROCESS — the in-memory executor slot is the singleton guard.

The background pass (`SessionLedgerImporter.poll_once`) walks every enabled PULLING source from its persisted byte-offset cursor to current end-of-data, running the discover -> read -> persist pipeline that ingests raw vendor session JSONL into the `__session` / `__event` store; per-source polling-lease acquisition, `LeaseHeartbeat` refresh, route-batch finalization, and per-session failure isolation all live inside `poll_once` (unchanged). One fire drains the whole visible backlog; new records are picked up on the next `*/5` cron fire. Per-pass counts (sources_polled, sessions_seen, events_persisted, batches_failed) are logged at drain completion — they are NOT returned, because the pass runs asynchronously.

WHY fire-and-forget: the action queue's serial `_poll_once` loop AWAITS each dispatched handler to completion before advancing, so an INLINE importer pass parks fleet-wide `process_call` dispatch for the pass's whole duration. The first pass after new filesystem sources became eligible was the source's entire ~1.2M-event history, run synchronously — which wedged dispatch fleet-wide until this verb was made the heartbeat. trigger_poll is the third instance of the reviewed heartbeat/drainer pattern (`summarize_quiescent_sessions` and `drain_event_embeddings` are the other two). For a SYNCHRONOUS single-source pass with a raising failure channel use `poll_source` instead; to install the periodic cron use `ensure_periodic_poll_schedule`.

EDGE_SINK (terminal/headless) — no `result_processor_customizations` / `error_processor_customizations`; the cron-fired action short-circuits at the EDGE_SINK_SKIP branch in `action_queue_poller`. See `21_scheduling_service/01_template_flow_record_lifecycle.md` for the terminal-cron pattern and `21_scheduling_service/02_action_queue_fast_return_contract.md` for the fast-return dispatch contract this verb now honors.
embedding_description: Cron-fired heartbeat that starts a singleton background importer-poll drainer over ALL enabled PULLING session-ledger sources, ingesting raw vendor session JSONL (discover -> read -> persist) from each source's persisted byte-offset cursor to end-of-data. Each fire submits one background pass to a single-slot executor and returns immediately with poller=started or poller=already_running, doing the whole poll off the serial action-queue dispatch path so a large first-run history backfill cannot wedge process_call dispatch fleet-wide. Poll counts are logged at completion, not returned. Unlike poll_source (one source, synchronous, raising) it polls all sources and silently skips a contended one; installed on a */5 cron by ensure_periodic_poll_schedule.
